Meeting records Transcript 
Summary
Gabor Kerekes and Amir Houieh decided to establish a single source of truth for engineering principles and skills, starting with "first principles," which Gabor Kerekes will organize in a new "engineering principles" repository. They discussed managing GitHub access for the repository and addressed the complexities of using professional and non-professional accounts. The participants outlined the necessary tasks for the website launch, including finalizing the manifesto, creating landing page copy, migrating articles, and deployment, with Amir Houieh tasked with finalizing design details like the menu. Gabor Kerekes and Amir Houieh finalized the manifesto, discussing website design elements such as text formatting, font size, spacing, and tracking for improved readability.
Details
Integration of Engineering Principles and Skills Gabor Kerekes and Amir Houieh discussed integrating an "engineering constitution" and shared cloud documents for rules and standards, suggesting using Gemini due to its coverage (00:00:00). They decided to establish a single source of truth starting with "first principles," which will cover topics like security and general programming approaches (00:04:47). They plan to organize this in a repo with one root file for principles and a separate folder for specific "skills," like structured thinking, ensuring the knowledge is shared within the team. Amir Houieh suggested a guiding principle to "do not do premature optimization" (00:06:00). Gabor Kerekes decided to create a minimal setup called "engineering principles" and planned to put it on a repo (00:07:23) (00:15:51).
GitHub Access and Security Gabor Kerekes and Amir Houieh discussed setting up GitHub access for the new repository. Gabor Kerekes clarified that themself and Amir Houieh already had access and asked about Amir Houieh’s preferred GitHub account, noting that the separation between professional and non-professional accounts might be complicated due to organizational access and private repositories (00:09:20). Gabor Kerekes mentioned using Arc and a password manager to simplify logging in on different devices (00:13:17).
Website Launch and Task Planning Gabor Kerekes outlined tasks for the new website launch, which they planned to document in Linear (00:15:51). The required steps include finalizing the manifesto, creating the copy for the landing page, copying all articles from the old site, and deployment (00:15:51). Amir Houieh was also tasked with finalizing the design details, such as the menu and navigation. Gabor Kerekes questioned the necessity of a footer for the website, suggesting it might be outdated (00:19:25).
Finalizing the Manifesto The participants agreed to finalize the manifesto, which is currently on Notion (00:22:17). Gabor Kerekes located the V1 manifesto in R&D Common. They discussed reading the manifesto in the format it would appear on the website and debated aspects of the website's design, including text formatting, font size, and spacing. Gabor Kerekes noted that the base font size should be 13 pixels, but the current configuration made the number of words per line too few (00:23:38). They also discussed and expressed a preference for "leading none" and adjusting the tracking for better readability (00:27:37).
Suggested next steps
Gabor Kerekes will create a repo with a minimal file for engineering principles and a folder for skills, and send it to GitHub.
Gabor Kerekes will put the website launch on the task list on Linear.
Gabor Kerekes will make the copy for the landing page, copy all the articles from the old website, and work on the deployment of the new website.
